spans.text: Servants of law and goodness that serve gods and powerful divine beings, swelling the ranks of their armies as soldiers, commanders and messengers.
Archons thrive off the energy of the upper planes they originate from, and so do not require food or drink.
All archons can spend one minute concentrating on teleportation to any location they wish on the same plane, and if they succeed they do so as though by the

spell without any chance for mishaps. An archon can only target themselves with this effect when invoked, but a group of archons can wordlessly coordinate their teleportation to arrive at the same location. Beginning this period of concentration is a bonus action.

If an archon meets their demise outside their native plane, they reform in their plane of origin after a single day. However, if destroyed in their native plane or by eidolic weapons, an archon does not return. The Eidolon or divine being they were in service to may choose to restore their life, but they will reappear in a lesser rank. Furthermore, an archon destroyed in their native plane or by eidolic weapons risks fracturing their divine essence, and could become an asura that reformed within another plane, possibly with new motivations and alliances.

Archons come in various forms. Like the fiends they fight, they could find themselves transformed or promoted through the ranks by higher beings, or by amassing enough power. Archons that exist for a long period of time evolve naturally, gaining new forms that eventually match their divine purpose.
From the lowest rank to the highest, archons exist in order of lantern, hound, warden, justice, word, sword, lion, crystal, trumpet, throne, and justice.

Unless dealing with a being of pure evil or a specific target it has been sent to battle, archons detest fighting and will avoid it at all cost. They see combat as a last resort as long as there is a possibility for any kind of diplomacy. Flipping to the other extreme, they are ruthless once they engage in combat and strike with deadly intent when their weapons are let loose.
